questions.def: Use the past simple tense for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to the cinema last night.

questions.def: Past continuous describes an action in progress in the past.
questions.question: She ___ a book when I called her.

questions.def: 'He' requires 'doesn't' instead of 'don't'.
questions.question: He don't like to eat meat.

questions.def: Present perfect is used for actions that started in the past and continue.
questions.question: They ___ at the factory for five years.

questions.def: Use present perfect with 'yet' for unfinished actions.
questions.question: I ___ my homework yet.

questions.def: Past perfect for an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: By the time she arrived, the movie ___.

questions.def: Future simple 'will' for future predictions or decisions.
questions.question: He ___ in London next year.

questions.def: Past continuous interrogative form. 'Were' because of 'you'.
questions.question: What ___ you ___ at 8 pm last night?

questions.def: 'Will' for predictions about the future.
questions.question: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.

questions.def: Present continuous for planned future arrangements.
questions.question: I ___ my friend tomorrow.

questions.def: Present simple for habitual actions (every morning).
questions.question: She ___ coffee every morning.

questions.def: Past simple 'went' for completed action with implied time.
questions.question: He ___ to the store earlier.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for action that started and continues.
questions.question: I ___ for you for an hour!

questions.def: 'They' requires the plural form 'were'.
questions.question: They ___ happy when they won the game.

questions.def: Second conditional 'if I were' (subjunctive mood).
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would study harder.

questions.def: 'Was born' is the correct past passive form.
questions.question: He ___ born in 1990.

questions.def: Past continuous: ongoing action interrupted by another action.
questions.question: I ___ TV when the phone rang.

questions.def: Reported speech: 'will' changes to 'would'.
questions.question: She told me she ___ to the party.

questions.def: Use past simple 'saw' with 'yesterday'.
questions.question: I ___ him yesterday.

questions.def: Present perfect with 'already'. 'Has' agrees with 'she'.
questions.question: She ___ already ___ her homework.

questions.def: Future perfect for action completed before a time in future.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ English for five years.

questions.def: Past continuous for action in progress at a specific time.
questions.question: We ___ dinner when you called.

questions.def: Second conditional. Use 'were' even for 'I'.
questions.question: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.

questions.def: Past reporting verb requires past tense in reported speech.
questions.question: He said that he ___ tired.

questions.def: Past perfect tense is used for an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: I ___ my homework before I watched TV.

questions.def: "Is going to" expresses a future plan or arrangement.
questions.question: She ___ to the party tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Has eaten' is the present perfect form, showing a completed action.
questions.question: He ___ breakfast already.

questions.def: Past perfect indicates an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: By the time we arrived, the movie ___ .

questions.def: "Haven't seen" is present perfect, referring to a period from past to now.
questions.question: I ___ him since last year.

questions.def: 'Have been waiting' describes an action continuing over a period of time.
questions.question: I ___ for you for an hour!
